question: A firefighter, a stock picker and four others trust their gut at work every day. Whose hunches have earned it?
answer: Those whose world repeats and whose mistakes show fast. Kahneman and Klein, long on opposite sides, agreed that a hunch becomes skill only with regular patterns and quick, clear feedback. Fires, chess and the operating theatre give both. Markets, hiring and politics give neither, so confidence grows while accuracy stays put.
move: Trust a hunch only where you have been told quickly when it was wrong.
ask: In which part of my life do I get fast feedback, and where am I trusting a hunch that has never been checked?

items.verdict: Thousands of games, each one scored the moment it ends.

items.verdict: Never sees how the rejected would have done, so the hunch is never corrected.

items.note: Calls an election three years out.
items.verdict: In Tetlock's 20-year study, experts' long-range calls did little better than chance.

reference: Kahneman and Klein, Conditions for Intuitive Expertise: A Failure to Disagree, American Psychologist 64:515, 2009; Tetlock, Expert Political Judgment, Princeton University Press, 2005
